sections.h2: Sugar yield from bagasse depends heavily on the cane variety

chart.title: Sugar yield varied by a factor of two across 115 cane varieties
chart.sub: Sugar released after pretreatment plus enzymes, g per 100 g dry matter.
chart.source: Study of 115 sugarcane varieties, as reported in the post.

sections.means: Pretreatment and variety set how much sugar comes out, and none of these lab yields has been costed.
sections.todo: Test the highest-yielding varieties in a pilot pretreatment and enzyme run before any plant is built.

sections.h2: Lab foams from bagasse polyol reached 0.32–0.48 MPa at the hotter cook

chart.title: Hotter cooks gave the strongest lab foams, at 0.32–0.48 MPa
chart.sub: Compressive strength of foams made from bagasse polyol, MPa; each range spans bagasse-to-solvent ratios from 1/2 to 1/4.

sections.means: The foams are small-batch lab results from one study, with no independent replication found.
sections.todo: Make foams in a larger batch, with thermal and replicate tests, before any commercial polyol is replaced.

sections.h2: Mills already burn bagasse, so a polyol plant competes with the boiler

chart.title: Mills already burn bagasse in cogeneration, 9,806 MW at the end of 2024
chart.sub: Installed bagasse cogeneration capacity, MW. The two figures differ in date and scope and are not additive.
chart.source: MNRE data reported in trade press; ministry table, July 2026.

sections.means: Most bagasse is burned for steam and power, so a polyol plant would have to replace that fuel and power.
sections.todo: Publish the price a polyol plant would need to pay to cover the lost fuel and export power.
